title: Monte Fontana Secca
clean:
In November nineteen seventeen, the front line of the First World War came up this mountain. A century later, the cows are coming back.

You're on the high pastures of the Monte Grappa massif, between the peaks of Monte Valderoa, Monte Solarolo and Monte Fontana Secca. Look around for the low stone buildings of the malga, the summer dairy farm, and then look out. On a clear day the view runs down the valley of the Piave all the way to the Venetian lagoon.

These hundred and fifty hectares of meadow and woodland were given away in twenty fifteen by Bruno and Liliana Collavo, to be looked after and opened to visitors, in memory of their parents, Aldo Collavo and Erminia Secco.

But first, the war. After the defeat at Caporetto in the autumn of nineteen seventeen, Italy's line fell back to the Grappa and the Piave. On the twenty-first and twenty-second of November, the summit here was taken by the Austro-German army, after it had been defended by the Alpine troops of the Vallecamonica battalion. If you walk the paths you'll still find trenches, tunnels and memorial stones. The ridge route that links them is called the Alta Via degli Eroi, the High Way of the Heroes, and it leads to the great war memorial on the summit of Cima Grappa.

[beat]

What's happening here is quietly ambitious. Not preserving a ruin, but bringing a working mountain farm back to life, with no mains water and no mains electricity. The old herdsman's house has been restored and opened as a place to tell the story of the mountain, with a film narrated by the actress Michela Cescon. The old stalls have been rebuilt to welcome visitors. And the pastures are meant for the Burlina, a cow found nowhere but the Veneto, and close to disappearing.

Up here the dairy makes the local mountain cheeses, Morlacco and Bastardo.

Before you come, check what's open, because the work is still going on. And then walk a stretch of the Alta Via degli Eroi. It's an extraordinary thing, to stand in a meadow full of cows and see a line of trenches running through it.

'Burlina found nowhere but the Veneto' paraphrases FAI's 'only native Veneto breed'.
Opening status is uncertain (the Stallone was due summer 2026), so the script tells listeners to check.
